labour_shares.source: Penn World Table 11.0, labsh, via FRED
labour_shares.units_input: Annual ratio, at current national prices, not seasonally adjusted.
labour_shares.units_plot: Percent of GDP. Compensation includes the estimated labour income of self-employed workers.
labour_shares.transformation: Multiply by 100; no smoothing or interpolation; retain missing observations as gaps.
labour_shares.interpretation: Descriptive historical series, not a causal estimate of automation or generative AI.

computer_income_share.source: C. Jones and Tonetti (May 2026), Figure 2, printed page 14, PDF page 15; BLS (2024).
computer_income_share.units: Share of private business value added paid to IT capital, percent; not purchases of computers, investment/GDP, technology-company profits, or all capital income.
computer_income_share.transformation: Recover all 37 annual vertices from the native vector curve in Figure 2. Calibrate against its year and percent tick marks; round to six decimals. No smoothing, interpolation of missing years, or extrapolation. Values reproduce the published curve, rather than newly downloaded BLS microdata.
computer_income_share.vintage: Historical evidence as reported in the May 2026 working paper; not a claim about the post-2023 AI boom.
computer_income_share.precision: Approximate values recovered from plotted vector coordinates; extra decimals preserve curve geometry and are not statistical precision.
computer_income_share.transistor_comparison: Paper, printed page 14: 100 million times more transistors on a computer chip than in the 1970s; an order-of-magnitude illustration, not a separate measured series in this figure.
computer_income_share.price_quantity_exposition: Classroom P is remuneration per unit of effective computing services and Q is their quality-adjusted volume; P times Q is income paid to IT capital, not computer manufacturers' sales. The denominator is total private-business value added. The post-2000 share decline means P times Q grows more slowly than that denominator, not necessarily that nominal P times Q falls. The price/quantity and scarcity explanation is the paper's interpretation, not a separate causal decomposition estimated from this plotted series.

theory.conditions: Strong complementarity across tasks (elasticity below one), fixed task allocation for the better-machine comparative static. Not every worker benefits; labour-share changes and wage changes are distinct.
